name: Prasiolite (Green Amethyst)
physical: Traditionally associated with a refreshed feeling
Crystal healers link it to relaxation and ease
Many people keep it nearby for comfort in stressful times
summary: Prasiolite, or green amethyst, is a soft mint-green quartz linked in crystal tradition with heart healing, renewal, gentle calm and compassionate growth.
intro: Prasiolite is a pale leek- or mint-green variety of quartz, delicate and cool in tone, and it is often called green amethyst even though that name is technically misleading. Natural prasiolite is very uncommon; most gems on the market are amethyst heated to around 500 degrees Celsius until it turns green, a treatment that has been used for decades. A few natural localities, including Montezuma in Brazil and parts of Poland, produce small amounts naturally. Faceted stones look fresh and clean in jewelry, and the soft color pairs well with silver and white metals.
history: The name prasiolite comes from the Greek prason, meaning leek, for its color. Green quartz was known to early gem dealers who sometimes called it by older names such as prase. The most famous source was a mine in Montezuma, Brazil, where amethyst turned green naturally due to volcanic heating. In the 20th century commercial heat treatment of Brazilian amethyst made the stone broadly available. Because the green variety has a short documented history, its metaphysical reputation is mostly modern, drawing on the heart-centered symbolism of green stones.
meaning: Prasiolite is considered a stone of the heart in crystal tradition, bringing the soothing calm of amethyst into the gentler, restorative color of green. Practitioners say it opens the heart chakra softly and is a good stone for people healing from heartbreak, loss or burnout. It is associated with self-acceptance, forgiveness and learning to let compassion lead. In meditation it is used to connect the heart with intuition, encouraging decisions rooted in kindness. It is also considered a stone of renewal, suited for new chapters, gardening or time in nature. Many find it less intense than emerald or malachite, making it a good fit for sensitive people and beginners. Physical associations are modest: a refreshed, relaxed feeling.
howToUse: Hold a faceted piece or smooth palm stone over your heart for a few minutes of slow breathing. Place prasiolite near a houseplant or on a garden altar to link it with growth. Wear it as a pendant on days that call for patience with yourself and others. Keep a tumbled stone beside your bed for evening reflection. Add it to a heart chakra grid with rose quartz and green aventurine. Carry a small piece when you are working through a transition or difficult conversation.
care: Prasiolite is quartz, so rinsing in cool water is fine, though the color can fade under strong sunlight, so keep it away from sunny windows. Heat can also alter the color, so avoid hot cars and radiators. Cleanse it with moonlight, sound, smoke or a selenite plate. Dry with a soft cloth and store it apart from harder gems. Avoid steam cleaners and harsh chemicals, which may dull the polish or stress any fractures.
identify: Natural prasiolite is a pale, slightly yellow-green, usually without the vivid saturation of dyed stones. Heat-treated amethyst turned green looks very similar, and the two cannot easily be told apart without lab tests. Intense, grassy green quartz is typically irradiated, dyed or glass. Genuine pieces scratch glass and show natural inclusions. Lab-grown green quartz exists. Because most green amethyst is treated, it is wise to ask a seller whether the stone is heat-treated or natural.

faq.q: Is prasiolite the same as green amethyst?
faq.a: Yes, the names are used for the same green quartz. The term green amethyst is common in the trade, though it is technically a misnomer, since the stone is usually heat-treated amethyst or naturally occurring green quartz.

Crystal healers use prasiolite for heart healing, forgiveness and renewal. It is considered a gentle stone, suited for self-acceptance and calm, and many people keep it near them during times of change.
